children: Shares of Mukesh Ambani-owned Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) have now become ones with the biggest exposure in the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book, following its biggest single-day gain in six years on Monday, November 2, according to latest data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Data available as of closing on November 2 shows the exposure for Reliance Industries surging to ₹4,711 crore, which is a 60% jump from the ₹2,937 crore figure reported as of closing on October 30.

With this, Reliance Industries has dethroned HDFC Bank from the top of the MTF book, a position it occupied for many months. India's largest private lender is now a distant second in the MTF book, with its leveraged exposure slipping below the ₹3,000 crore mark to ₹2,991 crore as of November 2.

The latest data shows the overall MTF book size to be ₹1.45 lakh crore, of which, the concentration among top 10 stocks at ₹19,442 crore. Within the top 10 names, Reliance Industries has a 24% share, after the jump seen on Monday.

Shares of Reliance Industries gained nearly 12% on Monday, November 2, in response to their September quarter results, that not only surpassed estimates, but were strong and led by their core O2C business. This was the biggest single-day gain seen by the stock since April 2020.
The move seen in Reliance Industries on Monday contributed to 44% of the Nifty 50's rally to start the week on a positive note.

Reliance Industries has also remained the most traded stock on the Nifty 500 index across both Monday and Tuesday. While Monday's session saw turnover of over ₹11,000 crore, Tuesday's turnover was in excess of ₹5,000 crore. Tuesday's session also saw delivery buying worth nearly ₹3,000 crore, following Monday's delivery buy figure of over ₹6,000 crore.
53% of the Reliance Industries shares traded on Tuesday were marked for delivery.

With this result, Reliance Industries has also become a "consensus buy" stock among analysts who track it, as all 33 now have a "buy" rating on the stock. The consensus estimates of price targets still imply a 21% upside from current levels.

The move seen on Reliance Industries on Monday resulted in the stock closing above its 20, 50 and 100-Day Moving Average (DMA). The next level on the upside is the 200-DMA level close to the ₹1,327. The move also added $8.5 billion to Chairman and Managing Director Mukesh Ambani's wealth, making him the richest man in Asia.

Shares of Reliance Industries saw a sharp recovery from the lows of the day to end 0.6% higher on Tuesday at ₹1,307.9. In case the stock does manage to hold on to the 12% gains through the month of November, it will mark the best month for the stock since April 2025.

title: Reliance Industries shares are now biggest in the MTF book after 60% jump in a single session
